bib.title: RankPrompt: Step-by-Step Comparisons Make Language Models Better Reasoners

read.skipped: References skimmed only; paper has no appendix

question: How can an LLM select the best of several sampled reasoning paths without a trained verifier or plain majority voting, especially when candidate answers disagree?
hypothesis: Comparing candidate reasoning paths step by step, with automatically built comparison exemplars, ranks them better than scoring each independently or voting on final answers.
contributions: RankPrompt: step-aware comparison instruction plus automatically generated comparison exemplars for LLM self-ranking
Gains on 11 arithmetic, commonsense, symbolic and BBH tasks with ChatGPT and GPT-4
74.33% agreement with human preference on AlpacaEval
Analysis of exemplar correctness, complexity, candidate number and order robustness

method.summary: Stage 1 samples n few-shot CoT reasoning paths. Stage 2 prompts the same LLM with a step-by-step comparison instruction and one auto-built comparison exemplar to pick the best candidate. Exemplars are comparison chains from Zero Ranking kept only if they reach the correct answer on a labeled question.

datasets.name: AQUA-RAT, ASDiv, GSM8K, SVAMP, ARC Challenge, CommonsenseQA, StrategyQA, Last Letter Concatenation
datasets.split: test set; validation set for CommonsenseQA

AlpacaEval
datasets.size: 805 instructions, each with a pair of responses and 4 human preferences

inference.decoding: temperature sampling for candidates; CoT baseline greedy
inference.temperature: 0.7 for candidates; 0 for CoT Prompting baseline; ranking temperature null
inference.samples: 5 candidates per question; 3 shuffled-order ranking runs for the order-robustness test; single run otherwise (null seeds)
inference.prompting: few-shot CoT prompts of Wei et al. 2022b and Suzgun et al. 2023 for candidates; ranking template (Table 2) with one task-specific comparison exemplar

parameters.exemplar_selection: comparison chain from Zero Ranking that reaches the correct answer

other.api_dates: experiments run between August 1, 2023 and October 1, 2023

metrics.name: human agreement
metrics.definition: agreement rate with the majority of human preferences on AlpacaEval

metrics.name: Oracle
metrics.definition: upper bound: correct if any candidate is correct

eval.protocol: single run per cell, no significance test or seeds reported

prompts.text: [Comparison Instruction] You are provided with a question and a series of potential responses. Your assignment involves a systematic, step-by-step comparison of the reasoning paths embedded within each response. This entails a thorough evaluation of each step's correctness and logical consistency. After completing this all-encompassing assessment, rank the responses in accordance with the soundness of their respective reasoning paths. Finally, select the best response and present it on a separate line as the optimal solution. [Comparison Example] {Comparison Exemplars} [Question] {Question} [Candidate Answers] {Candidates} [Comparison] Let's compare the answers step by step.

limits: Only proprietary models (gpt-3.5-turbo, gpt-4) tested; authors concede this
Comparison exemplars enlarge context and API cost
Single run per cell, no variance or significance reported
CoT baseline is one greedy sample while others use 5 sampled candidates at temp 0.7, so compute is not matched
Exemplar needs labeled data with correct answer (minimal, one per task)
Ranking-stage temperature, max tokens and exact exemplars not given; no code link in the text
Gains on ARC are tiny (87.42 vs Zero Ranking 87.57)
